title: Embeddings consistency briefing and self-serve checklist (draft)
content:
SUMMARY (one-line ready for status page):
Users may observe intermittent inconsistent embedding vectors for short-lived requests in us-west-2 between 2029-06-19 22:10 UTC and 2029-06-20 05:42 UTC. We mitigated the primary cause and implemented rolling validation; we continue verification and offer a self-serve replay/checklist for impacted tenants.

INTENDED AUDIENCE: Customers who consume Redwood embeddings (hosted API and Dedicated) and partner integrations that index embeddings for search/ranking. This is a customer-facing draft intended for posting to the status page and sending to impacted accounts.

INCIDENT FACTS (concise):
- Impact window: 2029-06-19 22:10 UTC -> 2029-06-20 05:42 UTC.
- Services affected: embeddings endpoint (v1/embeddings), some streaming-generation sessions that trigger inline embedding calls.
- Symptom: occasional mismatched/unstable embedding vectors for identical inputs, primarily for sequences >256 tokens or with non-ASCII whitespace characters.
- Scope: ~0.9% of total embedding requests in us-west-2 during the window; concentrated to a subset of tenants with long-context embeddings or custom tokenization pipelines.
- Customer-visible: search result rank jitter, small delta in similarity scores, occasional failed similarity threshold checks.

STATUS PAGE COPY (short):
Redwood Inference is investigating an issue impacting a subset of embeddings requests in us-west-2 that may lead to inconsistent vectors for identical inputs. We have deployed mitigations and validation checks; we will post a final update after full verification. If you rely on embeddings for indexing or parity-sensitive workflows, follow the self-serve checklist below or contact your CSM for assistance.

TECHNICAL SUMMARY (non-PII, for customers wanting details):
Root cause (high-level): During a recent kernel update to the quantized embedding runtime we introduced a regression in tokenization normalization when non-standard whitespace characters were present. This led to an off-by-one alignment between tokenizer and model kv-caching for some code paths, producing slightly different float outputs for the same logical input. The issue surfaced only on sequences exceeding typical prefix lengths and in an edge interaction with our continuous batching heuristics.
What we did:
- Rolled back the kernel change on affected inference hosts within 40 minutes of detection.
- Deployed alignment validation (tokenizer->embedding->checksum) across all us-west-2 workers.
- Replayed buffered requests where possible and flagged suspect outputs in logs for downstream verification.
- Triggered a targeted rebuild of our quantized kernel with an additional normalization boundary test.

What remains: ongoing cross-region verification and a small percentage of customers still require explicit replay of data indexed during the window. We are also evaluating an additional automated re-embedding job for customers that opt in.

IMPACTED TENANT INDICATORS (how you can tell):
- Increased similarity score variance in recent queries (compared to baseline).
- Search results where expected top-k changed between queries made before and after 2029-06-20 05:42 UTC.
- If you see logs with tokenization warnings: "token-alignment-check-failed" (we inserted this marker during mitigation).

CUSTOMER SELF-SERVE CHECKLIST (recommended sequence):
1) Confirm exposure: Run a small parity test: pick 10 representative inputs you index, call /v1/embeddings with same model and params, compare cosine similarity across runs separated by >24h. If any identical input returns vectors with cosine similarity < 0.9992, mark as suspect.
2) Temporary mitigation: If you use a similarity threshold gating writes, consider adding a thin buffer window (e.g., allow reindex within 2 minutes) or flagging near-threshold writes for manual review.
3) Replay guidance: If you confirm mismatch, request a replay package via support form (see How to request below). The replay process will: (a) provide a signed evidence bundle of original requests (request ids + timestamps), (b) offer a one-time free re-embedding run on request (subject to data retention limits), (c) provide checksums pre and post re-embed.
4) Long-term: Consider running a periodic background parity job (nightly small-sample re-embed) to detect regressions earlier. Our Optimize team can share a lightweight script for Dedicated customers.

HOW TO REQUEST HELP / REPLAY (steps for customers):
- Fill the support form at https://support.redwood.ai/incident-replay with: tenant-id, approximate index time window, representative input(s), and preferred contact.
- If you prefer enterprise handling, ask your CSM to open JIRA INC-8792 for a prioritized replay and remediation plan.
- Attach any internal evidence (snapshots, baseline vectors) if available. We will assign a partner engineer and provide an evidence package back within 48 hours.

SLA & CREDITS:
Customers with SLA-covered Dedicated contracts may be eligible for service credits if the incident triggers an SLO breach. Eligibility requires documented impact (we will accept your evidence bundle plus our internal request logs). For Hosted customers we are offering a one-time re-embed for verified impact; contact support for details.

TIMELINE (UTC, consolidated):
- 2029-06-19 22:10 — anomaly detection alert (similarity variance metric)
- 2029-06-19 22:35 — mitigation flag inserted; tokenization-check marker enabled for new requests
- 2029-06-19 23:12 — rollback of quantized kernel on ~60% of affected hosts
- 2029-06-20 00:30 — full rollback complete; alignment validation running
- 2029-06-20 02:05 — targeted revalidation and replay pipeline started for buffered requests
- 2029-06-20 05:42 — verification threshold met; incident moved to monitoring/verification
- 2029-06-21 10:00 — customer-facing postmortem draft (this document)

EVIDENCE & VERIFICATION:
We will provide an evidence bundle for each replay request that includes: request ids, approximate timestamps, original vector checksums (where available), and server-side alignment logs. For privacy, payload contents are not included unless customers explicitly opt in.

COMMUNICATION PLAN / SUGGESTED STATUSPAGE POSTS:
1) Initial short notice (already posted): "Investigating issues affecting a subset of embedding requests in us-west-2."
2) Post-mitigation (ready now): "Mitigations deployed; validation in progress. If you rely on embeddings for indexing, please run the short parity checklist or request a replay."
3) Final closure (after verification): Provide a short technical summary, tenant-level impact list for those who requested evidence, and steps taken to prevent recurrence. Include SLA credit/process notes where applicable.

OPEN ACTIONS (internal, visible to customers):
- [REDWOOD] Provide evidence bundle and replay options to each requesting tenant (owner: Marco Ruiz, ETA 48h).
- [REDWOOD] Publish kernel regression test to public runbook and add to model-onboarding checklist (owner: Applied ML).
- [CUSTOMER] Run parity checklist and raise support ticket if mismatch confirmed.
- [REDWOOD] Offer scheduled re-embed window for Dedicated customers who opt in (ops calendar to be coordinated by Aisha Patel).

RISK & FOLLOW-UPS:
We estimate the chance of recurrence from the same root cause as low after the rollback and new validation checks, but we will monitor tokenization alignment and continuous-batching interactions for 30 days. We will share a final postmortem with metrics and code-level fixes once internal RCA completes.

CONTACTS:
- Primary CS contact: Claire Zhang (claire@redwood.ai)
- Partner/AE escalation: Daniel Moreno (daniel@redwood.ai)
- Technical lead (embedded inference): Marco Ruiz (marco@redwood.ai)

APPENDIX: quick parity script (high-level):
- curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" -d '{"model":"embed-large-v2","input": "<your-sample>" }'
- compute cosine and compare to baseline. If you want the small script we used for validation, request it from support and we'll share as a Gist or private repo for Dedicated customers.

NOTES: This draft intentionally balances customer-facing simplicity with enough technical detail for engineering teams. Please review and suggest edits to the status copy before publishing.

Document history: draft prepared by Claire Zhang; reviewed by Marco Ruiz and Aisha Patel; awaiting legal sign-off for SLA language.
